newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs fear CPI, brace for correction.
newsitem.headline: OLOs fear CPI, brace for correction.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds were firmer in quiet early business with Bunds but traders feared that a higher-than-expected CPI at 1230 GMT would trigger selling pressure.
At 0825 GMT, the benchmark 2006 OLO yielded 6.47 percent, against 6.49 percent late on Thursday.
The yield spread with German 10-year paper was unchanged at 22 basis points after earlier touching 21.
But traders said Belgian OLOs were "very expensive". "Why not invest more in German paper?" said one, noting that the spread for shorter-term OLOs was considerably smaller.

One trader said the market had so far been ignoring ongoing government talks on the 1997 budget but any bad news would spark a sell-off which could send the 10-year bond yield soaring to 7.00 percent.
"Everybody's supposing that (Prime Minister) Dehaene will again fix it all, but if problems should arise, or when we get closer to the EMU launch date, OLOs could see some problems."
But for now, OLOs remained supported, which especially showed when the market weakened.
"We immediately see some bottom-picking...it shows there is still a lot of money available," he said.
Traders said Belgium would start lagging the U.S. if the U.S. rose any further.
They said business was slow and would not liven up before the 1230 GMT release of the U.S. CPI data.
